US President Donald Trump threatened military action against Iran for a rumored "dirty bomb" plot targeting Washington, saying: "If they do (that), we’re going to fight." He insisted his administration is closely monitoring Tehran and had extensive intelligence on its activities. "We will not allow that." ... - Denmark expels Russian defense attache, halts non-essential visas for Russians Denmark has ordered the Russian defense attache to leave within seven days and will halt all non-essential visas for Russian citizens, according to Foreign Minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen. He called the expulsion a strong signal to Moscow, adding "enough is enough," and said Denmark is continuing to support Ukraine. Rasmussen said the government plans to lift the obligation to receive ships linked to Russia and would discuss visa restrictions with other Schengen countries, singling out France, while Denmark will not expel all Russian diplomats as it needs to maintain communication with Moscow.

items.title: Reuters World News Summary | International
items.excerpt: Student protests held across Europe with demands from school funding to climate A fresh wave of student protests took place across Europe on Friday, inspired by demonstrations that rocked France but far more muted, with demands ranging from more funding for education to climate justice and even ​ending conscription. Organisers said they were holding an "international youth strike" in at least 25 countries, including Britain, Germany, Spain, Italy and Croatia. In Germany, campaign group "Gen Z regelt" — "Gen Z takes charge" in German — ‌said it was organising ​protests in 73 cities and towns. Spain to extend banking tax to fund housing policies, PM says Spain's Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez announced on Saturday his government would approve at Tuesday's cabinet meeting an extension of the current banking levy to 2027 to fund housing policies. Sanchez last month called a snap election for November 29 in a bid to harness the momentum from massive housing protests. Fire at power station in Iraq's Basra kills at least 4, injures 35 At least 4 people were killed and 35 injured in a fire at a power station in southern Iraq on Saturday, with the toll expected to rise, security officials said. Civil defence teams brought the fire at the Hartha power station north of Basra under control after firefighters responded to the incident, Iraq's state news agency, INA, reported. Houthi attacks add to worries over Trump Saudi nuclear power pact Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure are adding to concerns about US President ‌Donald Trump's proposed nuclear power pact with the kingdom, weeks before US senators are due to vote on whether to block the agreement. Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis have intensified drone and missile strikes on Saudi airports, oil facilities and office buildings, raising questions about Riyadh's ability to secure nuclear plants that would be built under the pact. States agree to UN talks aiming to regulate 'killer robots' by 2028 UN talks on regulating weapons with little or no human oversight ended on Saturday with a pledge for further discussions to develop new rules within two years, an outcome weakened by Russia's opposition and disappointing human rights groups. Proponents had called for legally binding rules within a short timeframe to regulate weapons systems that can identify and engage targets with varying degrees of autonomy, sometimes called "killer robots".

items.title: Democrats won big in the midterms. So now what? By Reuters
items.excerpt: WASHINGTON, Nov 21 (Reuters) - Democrats basking in their November 3 election wins will soon unveil an ambitious legislative agenda for the first 100 days and beyond, in a test of progressives’ influence and Republicans’ willingness to cooperate, as they take control of the US Congress on January 3. That agenda is likely to be unveiled in early December once a Senate leadership race is settled. It will mark a thunderous reversal of the past two years, when President Donald Trump’s Republicans ruled the Senate and House of Representatives. With their narrow majorities, they rammed through major tax cuts skewed toward the rich and stood by as Trump grabbed their powers over tariffs and spending. Democrats’ new majorities in Congress are anything but narrow. With a 56-44 majority in the Senate they are four votes short of the 60 votes needed to advance most legislation. In the House, their 257-172 force could grow beyond an 85-vote margin once a handful of races are settled. "This is a realignment," said Democratic Senator Raphael Warnock of Georgia in a post-election interview with reporters. But in a warning to Democrats, veteran Republican Senator John Boozman of Arkansas said in an interview that despite his party’s losses across the United States, Trump remains "a powerful force" and "I don’t see any of his vetoes getting overridden" by Congress during his remaining two years in office. AGGRESSIVE AGENDA For months, Democrats have been plotting a House-Senate coordinated attack to undo Trump’s major accomplishments, according to lawmakers and aides. With the high cost of living the top concern voiced by voters, Democratic leaders are going after the low-hanging fruit that also would help unite their party’s progressives and moderates. Early votes are expected on legislation handcuffing Trump’s ability to wage war on Iran without Congress’ approval, which would help lower gasoline prices. Reversing Republicans’ deep cuts to Medicaid and SNAP food stamp programs would begin helping the poor meet healthcare and grocery costs. Meanwhile, progressives have urged raising the federal minimum wage, which is unchanged since 2009 at $7.25 per hour. Some are pushing for $20 to $25. And in response to voter disgust over Washington ethics breaches, one of the first bills Democrats are expected to present is one barring lawmakers from insider trading of stocks. Republicans face a bind: joining Democrats could anger Trump unless he backs measures, while stonewalling could anger voters. "I think there’s a real understanding in Congress that things like healthcare, the really exorbitant premiums, you know, that people are having to pay" must be addressed, said Boozman, who was one of the Republicans who supported around $1 trillion in cuts to Medicare, Medicaid and Obamacare programs enacted last year. Boozman is one of the senators who would be up for re-election in 2028 and potentially open to cooperating with Democrats, although he said he would seek guidance from Trump. ... Newly elected progressives, who are growing in numbers in state and local offices, have a far deeper agenda for the next two years such as cutting off aid to Israel and placing a moratorium on new AI data centers. Their to-do list also includes revamping campaign finance rules, raising taxes on the rich, writing comprehensive immigration reform and mitigating the effects of climate change.

items.title: 2026 MAMA Awards Winners List: BTS & ENHYPEN Lead
items.excerpt: # BTS, ENHYPEN, BIGBANG & CORTIS Are Big Winners of 2026 MAMA Awards The K-pop awards were presented over the course of two nights in Osaka, Japan. ... BTS, ENHYPEN, BIGBANG and CORTIS were the big winners of the 2026 MAMA Awards, which were held Friday and Saturday (Nov. 20-21) at the Kyocera Dome Osaka, in Japan. The awards streamed live worldwide on CJ ENM’s Mnet Plus platform. BTS won artist of the year, best male group and album of the year for ARIRANG. They also ranked in the top 10 for fans’ choice male and song of the year for “SWIM.” ENHYPEN won fans’ choice of the year, favorite MCD Stage and also ranked in the top 10 for fans’ choice male. Both groups have topped the all-genre Billboard 200 album chart this year. BTS led for three weeks in April with ARIRANG. ENHYPEN was on top for one week in September with The Sin: Bliss. BIGBANG won music visionary of the year and best music video, and also ranked in the top 10 for fans’ choice male. Taeyang of BIGBANG also won best dance performance male solo with “LIVE FAST DIE SLOW.” CORTIS won song of the year and best dance performance male group with “REDRED.” CORTIS also ranked in the top 10 for fans’ choice male. Yeonjun of TOMORROW X TOGETHER won best male artist. The group also made the top 10 for fans’ choice male. Soyeon of i-dle won best female artist. That group also made the top 10 for fans’ choice female. ALPHA DRIVE ONE and TUIDE were co-winners for best new artist. Music released between Oct. 1, 2025, and Sept. 30, 2026 was eligible for this year’s awards.
